# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Pandey_2023_hydroxyurea"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Pandey_2023_hydroxyurea"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/psp4.12945> (open access; Appendix S1
  holds the model equations, Text S2, and the per-participant estimates,
  Tables S1-S4)
* Parent model paper: <https://doi.org/10.3390/pharmaceutics14051065>
  (Pandey 2022, open access; PK estimates in Table 2, cohort summaries of the
  pharmacodynamic estimates in Tables 3 and 5)

Pandey 2023 studies how missed hydroxyurea doses change two biomarkers of
response in sickle cell disease, mean cell volume (MCV) and fetal hemoglobin
(HbF). It reuses the integrated PK-PD model of Pandey 2022, which it reprints
in Text S2. Hydroxyurea is absorbed through a transit chain and eliminated
first-order; the daily average plasma concentration drives (i) a five-pool
erythropoiesis model in which the drug kills stem cells and lengthens red-cell
lifespan, (ii) a mean-cell-volume balance in which new cells are larger in
proportion to the concentration, and (iii) a two-step HbF induction model.
The authors fitted every participant separately by weighted least squares, so
the model has no between-subject variability or residual error. The packaged
typical values are the HUSTLE cohort central values printed in Pandey 2022;
the 2023 per-participant estimates are reproduced further below.

# Population

Pandey 2023 analysed 40 children and adolescents with sickle cell disease from
the HUSTLE trial (NCT00305175, St. Jude Children's Research Hospital) whose MCV
or HbF fell during treatment in a way their pharmacy refill records did not
explain. Participants receiving transfusions, with sparse or gapped data, or
whose biomarkers were already explained by the refill records were excluded.
The paper does not tabulate demographics for the 40. The parent analysis of 85
HUSTLE participants (Pandey 2022 Table 1) reports a starting age of 10.12
(SD 4.72) years, 54 male / 31 female, and baseline MCV 85.34 fL, MCH 29.76 pg,
HbF 8.0%, hematocrit 23.46% and red-cell count 2.777 x 10^6 cells/uL.

```{r population}
str(rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Pandey_2023_hydroxyurea"))$population)
```

# Typical participant and dosing

The figures below use one typical participant: a 30 kg, 135 cm boy with the
HUSTLE baseline hematocrit of 23.46%, taking 20 mg/kg (600 mg) once a day.
Pandey 2023 does not report the covariates, baselines or dose history of the
representative participant in its Figures 4-6, so the figures are reproduced
in shape rather than value.

```{r typical}
mod <- readModelDb("Pandey_2023_hydroxyurea")
ui <- rxode2::rxode(mod)
covs <- data.frame(WT = 30, HT = 135, SEXF = 0, HCT = 23.46)
dose_mg <- 20 * covs$WT

# Build a dosing history from the days on which a dose is taken, with a
# daily observation grid. Doses sort before observations at the same time,
# so the observation at day d carries day d's average concentration.
make_regimen <- function(id, label, dose_days, n_days) {
  doses <- data.frame(
    id = rep(id, length(dose_days)), time = dose_days, evid = rep(1L, length(dose_days)),
    amt = rep(dose_mg, length(dose_days)), cmt = rep("depot", length(dose_days))
  )
  obs <- data.frame(id = id, time = seq(0, n_days), evid = 0L, amt = 0, cmt = "central")
  dplyr::bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
    dplyr::mutate(regimen = label) |>
    dplyr::arrange(time, dplyr::desc(evid)) |>
    cbind(covs)
}
# A step cap below one day keeps LSODA from stepping across a day's sharp
# absorption peak on these multi-year daily-dosing courses; without it the
# solver can exhaust its step budget.
solve_days <- function(events, ...) {
  events <- dplyr::arrange(events, id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))
  sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = events, keep = "regimen", maxsteps = 1e6, hmax = 0.1, ...) |>
    as.data.frame()
  if (is.null(sim$id)) sim$id <- events$id[1]
  sim |> dplyr::filter(time == round(time))
}
```

# Pharmacokinetics

A single 20 mg/kg dose, the dose at which HUSTLE collected its PK profiles
(the PK estimates of Pandey 2022 were fitted to those profiles' NCA
summaries).

```{r pk-single}
pk_ev <- rbind(
  data.frame(id = 1L, time = 0, evid = 1L, amt = dose_mg, cmt = "depot"),
  data.frame(id = 1L, time = seq(0, 1, by = 1 / 480), evid = 0L, amt = 0, cmt = "central")
) |>
  cbind(covs)
pk <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = pk_ev, rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  dplyr::mutate(id = 1L, time_h = time * 24, treatment = "20 mg/kg single dose")

ggplot(pk, aes(time_h, Cc)) +
  geom_line() +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 12)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time after dose (h)", y = "Plasma hydroxyurea (ug/mL)",
    title = "Typical plasma concentration after a 20 mg/kg dose"
  )
```

## PKNCA validation

```{r pknca}
stopifnot(pk$time_h[1] == 0, all(!is.na(pk$Cc)))
# Floor the integrator's sub-atol undershoot in the far tail.
stopifnot(all(pk$Cc >= -1e-6 * max(pk$Cc)))
conc <- pk |>
  dplyr::mutate(Cc = pmax(Cc, 0)) |>
  dplyr::filter(time_h <= time_h[which.max(Cc)] | Cc >= 1e-6 * max(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time = time_h, Cc, treatment)
conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(
  data.frame(id = 1L, time = 0, amt = dose_mg, treatment = "20 mg/kg single dose"),
  amt ~ time | treatment + id
)
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = c(0, 0), end = c(8, Inf),
  auclast = c(TRUE, FALSE),
  cmax = c(FALSE, TRUE), tmax = c(FALSE, TRUE),
  aucinf.obs = c(FALSE, TRUE), half.life = c(FALSE, TRUE)
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
```

Pandey 2022 Table 1 reports the HUSTLE NCA means: AUC to the last sample
(8 h) 85.79, AUC to infinity 92.98 ug h/mL, Cmax 26.13 ug/mL, Tmax 0.82 h and
lambda_z 0.65 1/h (half-life ln 2 / 0.65 = 1.07 h).

```{r nca-compare}
published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment, ~cmax, ~tmax, ~auclast, ~aucinf.obs, ~half.life,
  "20 mg/kg single dose", 26.13, 0.82, 85.79, 92.98, log(2) / 0.65
)
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = published,
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(cmax = "ug/mL", tmax = "h", auclast = "ug*h/mL", aucinf.obs = "ug*h/mL", half.life = "h"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Typical-participant NCA vs. HUSTLE cohort means (Pandey 2022 Table 1). * differs by >20%.")

nca_wide <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  dplyr::select(PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES)
stopifnot(
  # Cmax and Tmax track the cohort means closely.
  abs(nca_wide$cmax / 26.13 - 1) < 0.10,
  abs(nca_wide$tmax / 0.82 - 1) < 0.25,
  # Exposure is within 30% of the cohort mean (see the narrative below).
  abs(nca_wide$aucinf.obs / 92.98 - 1) < 0.30
)
```

Cmax (`r signif(nca_wide$cmax, 3)` ug/mL) and Tmax
(`r signif(nca_wide$tmax, 2)` h) match the cohort means. The AUC is lower
(`r signif(nca_wide$aucinf.obs, 3)` vs. 92.98 ug h/mL) and the half-life
longer (`r signif(nca_wide$half.life, 3)` h, which is ln 2 / ke, vs. about
1.07 h from the mean lambda_z): AUC is
`F D / (ke Vp)`, so evaluating it at the mean `F` and mean `ke` of the
individual fits (a typical participant) is not the same as averaging
individual AUCs, and the comparison cohort spans a range of body sizes and
doses. The PK parameters were not tuned.

## Daily average concentration

The pharmacodynamics are driven by the daily average plasma concentration,
held constant for each dosing day. The model computes it in closed form as
`F D / (ke Vp)` divided by one day. Integrating the simulated plasma profile
over the dosing day must give the same number.

```{r cavg-check}
day1 <- pk |> dplyr::filter(time <= 1)
auc_day <- sum(diff(day1$time) * (head(day1$Cc, -1) + tail(day1$Cc, -1)) / 2)
mid <- which.min(abs(pk$time - 0.5))
cavg_model <- pk$Cavg[mid]
c(trapezoid_ug_per_mL = auc_day, model_Cavg = cavg_model, model_Cavg_uM = pk$Cavg_uM[mid])
# Same parameters on both sides: trapezoid error on a 3-minute grid plus the
# drug left in the body at 24 h (~exp(-13)); measured ~5e-6.
stopifnot(abs(auc_day / cavg_model - 1) < 1e-3)
```

# Steady states

Without drug every state stays at its baseline (the initial conditions are
the pre-treatment steady state). Under uninterrupted daily dosing the daily
average concentration is constant, so the long-run state solves algebraic
equations: `MCV = Vm0 + alpha C`, `Ci = kmet C / (Kmet + C) / kdi`,
`Fm = (kbf + kaf Ci^n / (Kaf^n + Ci^n)) / kdf`, and the red-cell count
satisfies `kpe(Ne) = (kte + kdse) kde Ne / kte`.

```{r steady-states}
nodrug <- make_regimen(1L, "no drug", dose_days = numeric(0), n_days = 1000)
s0 <- solve_days(nodrug)
th <- exp(ui$theta)
names(th) <- sub("^l", "", names(th))
stopifnot(
  max(abs(s0$RBC / th[["bl_rbc"]] - 1)) < 1e-6,
  max(abs(s0$MCV / th[["bl_mcv"]] - 1)) < 1e-6,
  max(abs(s0$hbf_mc / th[["bl_fm"]] - 1)) < 1e-6
)

daily <- make_regimen(1L, "daily", dose_days = seq(0, 2999), n_days = 3000)
s1 <- solve_days(daily)
last <- s1[s1$time == 2999, ]
C <- last$Cavg_uM
ci_ss <- th[["kmet"]] * C / (th[["kmmet"]] + C) / th[["kdi"]]
fm_ss <- (th[["kdf"]] * th[["bl_fm"]] +
  th[["kaf"]] * ci_ss^th[["hill_hbf"]] / (th[["kaf50"]]^th[["hill_hbf"]] + ci_ss^th[["hill_hbf"]])) / th[["kdf"]]
kde_ss <- th[["kdemax"]] * (1 - C / (th[["kde50"]] + C))
kdse_ss <- th[["kdsemax"]] * C / (th[["kdse50"]] + C)
prol0 <- th[["kdemax"]] * th[["bl_rbc"]] / th[["kte"]]
kpemax <- th[["kte"]] * prol0 * (th[["psi_rbc"]]^th[["gamma_rbc"]] + th[["bl_rbc"]]^th[["gamma_rbc"]]) /
  th[["psi_rbc"]]^th[["gamma_rbc"]]
rbc_ss <- uniroot(function(ne) {
  kpemax * th[["psi_rbc"]]^th[["gamma_rbc"]] / (th[["psi_rbc"]]^th[["gamma_rbc"]] + ne^th[["gamma_rbc"]]) -
    (th[["kte"]] + kdse_ss) * kde_ss * ne / th[["kte"]]
}, c(0.01, 10), tol = 1e-12)$root
ss <- data.frame(
  quantity = c("MCV (fL)", "Mean cell HbF (pg)", "RBC (10^12/L)"),
  simulated = c(last$MCV, last$hbf_mc, last$RBC),
  analytic = c(th[["bl_mcv"]] + th[["alpha_mcv"]] * C, fm_ss, rbc_ss)
)
knitr::kable(ss, digits = 4, caption = "Day-3000 state vs. analytic steady state, uninterrupted 20 mg/kg/day.")
stopifnot(all(abs(ss$simulated / ss$analytic - 1) < 1e-3))
```

# Missing doses on consecutive days (Figure 4)

Doses are missed in five blocks starting on days 250, 500, 1000, 1500 and
2000, each 0, 10, 40, 80 or 150 days long, over a 2320-day course. The
percentage of time below threshold (%tbt) uses the paper's illustrative
thresholds of 90 fL for MCV and 5 pg for mean cell HbF.

```{r figure-4}
n_days <- 2320
block_starts <- c(250, 500, 1000, 1500, 2000)
missed_blocks <- function(len) unlist(lapply(block_starts, function(s) s + seq_len(len) - 1))
lens <- c(0, 10, 40, 80, 150)
fig4_ev <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(lens), function(i) {
  days <- setdiff(seq(0, n_days - 1), missed_blocks(lens[i]))
  make_regimen(i, sprintf("%d consecutive days", lens[i]), days, n_days)
}))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(fig4_ev[, c("id", "time", "evid")]))
fig4 <- solve_days(fig4_ev) |>
  dplyr::mutate(regimen = factor(regimen, levels = sprintf("%d consecutive days", lens)))

tbt <- function(sim) {
  sim |>
    dplyr::group_by(regimen) |>
    dplyr::summarise(
      pct_miss = 100 * mean(Cavg[time < n_days] == 0),
      tbt_mcv = 100 * mean(MCV < 90),
      tbt_hbf = 100 * mean(hbf_mc < 5),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
}
plot_bio <- function(sim, title, caption) {
  sim |>
    dplyr::select(time, regimen, `MCV (fL)` = MCV, `Mean cell HbF (pg)` = hbf_mc, `Avg Cp (ug/mL)` = Cavg) |>
    tidyr::pivot_longer(-c(time, regimen)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(name = factor(name, levels = c("MCV (fL)", "Mean cell HbF (pg)", "Avg Cp (ug/mL)"))) |>
    ggplot(aes(time, value, colour = regimen)) +
    geom_line() +
    geom_hline(
      data = data.frame(name = factor(c("MCV (fL)", "Mean cell HbF (pg)"), levels = c("MCV (fL)", "Mean cell HbF (pg)", "Avg Cp (ug/mL)")), y = c(90, 5)),
      aes(yintercept = y), linetype = "dotted"
    ) +
    facet_wrap(~name, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
    labs(x = "Time (days)", y = NULL, colour = NULL, title = title, caption = caption)
}
plot_bio(fig4, "Missing the dose on consecutive days", "Replicates Figure 4 of Pandey 2023 (typical participant).")
fig4_tbt <- tbt(fig4)
fig4_tbt |>
  dplyr::rename(Regimen = regimen, "%miss" = pct_miss, "%tbt MCV" = tbt_mcv, "%tbt HbF" = tbt_hbf) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 0, caption = "Figure 4 regimens. Pandey 2023 reports %miss 0/2/9/17/32 with %tbt MCV 0/0/7/20/36 and HbF 0/0/0/11/28.")
```

```{r figure-4-checks}
# The %miss values follow from the design and must match the paper's.
stopifnot(all(abs(fig4_tbt$pct_miss - c(0, 2, 9, 17, 32)) < 1))
# Paper: %tbt for MCV is 0 for 10 consecutive missed days and grows with
# longer blocks. The simulation is deterministic (no random draws).
stopifnot(
  fig4_tbt$tbt_mcv[2] < 1,
  all(diff(fig4_tbt$tbt_mcv) >= 0),
  fig4_tbt$tbt_mcv[5] > fig4_tbt$tbt_mcv[3]
)
```

The 10-day blocks barely move either biomarker, while 80- and 150-day blocks
let MCV fall back towards its 85 fL baseline and spend a growing share of time
below 90 fL, as in Figure 4. The typical participant's baseline mean cell HbF
(2.4 pg) is below the 5 pg threshold, so %tbt for HbF also includes the first
weeks of treatment; the paper's representative participant started near 2 pg
as well.

# Interspersed vs. consecutive missed doses (Figure 5)

From day 200 a dose is missed after every four doses (4:1), compared with the
five 80-day blocks of Figure 4. Both miss about 400 doses (%miss 17-18).

```{r figure-5}
days_all <- seq(0, n_days - 1)
four_one <- days_all[!(days_all >= 200 & (days_all - 200) %% 5 == 4)]
fig5_ev <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  make_regimen(1L, "4:1 pattern", four_one, n_days),
  make_regimen(2L, "80 consecutive days", setdiff(days_all, missed_blocks(80)), n_days)
)
fig5 <- solve_days(fig5_ev)
plot_bio(fig5, "Interspersed vs. consecutive nonadherence", "Replicates Figure 5 of Pandey 2023 (typical participant).")
fig5_tbt <- tbt(fig5)
fig5_tbt |>
  dplyr::rename(Regimen = regimen, "%miss" = pct_miss, "%tbt MCV" = tbt_mcv, "%tbt HbF" = tbt_hbf) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 0, caption = "Figure 5 regimens. Pandey 2023 reports %tbt 0 (both biomarkers) for 4:1 and MCV 20 / HbF 11 for 80 consecutive days.")
four <- fig5_tbt[fig5_tbt$regimen == "4:1 pattern", ]
block <- fig5_tbt[fig5_tbt$regimen == "80 consecutive days", ]
stopifnot(
  abs(four$pct_miss - 18) < 1, abs(block$pct_miss - 17) < 1,
  # The paper's key finding: spread-out misses keep MCV above threshold,
  # consecutive misses do not.
  four$tbt_mcv < 1,
  block$tbt_mcv > 5
)
```

As in the paper, the same number of missed doses keeps MCV above 90 fL when
spread out and drops it below the threshold for weeks when taken as long
breaks.

# Daily adherence probability (Figure 6)

Each day the dose is taken with probability p, drawn once per regimen with R's
random number generator.

```{r figure-6}
set.seed(20230516)
probs <- c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1)
fig6_ev <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(probs), function(i) {
  taken <- days_all[stats::runif(length(days_all)) < probs[i]]
  make_regimen(i, sprintf("p = %.2f", probs[i]), taken, n_days)
}))
fig6 <- solve_days(fig6_ev) |>
  dplyr::mutate(regimen = factor(regimen, levels = sprintf("p = %.2f", probs)))
plot_bio(fig6, "Fixed daily probability of taking the dose", "Replicates Figure 6 of Pandey 2023 (typical participant).")
fig6_late <- fig6 |>
  dplyr::filter(time >= 1000) |>
  dplyr::group_by(regimen) |>
  dplyr::summarise(mean_mcv = mean(MCV), mean_hbf = mean(hbf_mc), .groups = "drop")
knitr::kable(fig6_late, digits = 1, caption = "Mean MCV and mean cell HbF after day 1000 by adherence probability.")
# MCV rises with adherence, roughly in proportion to the fraction of days
# dosed (the MCV equation is linear in the daily average concentration); the
# p = 1 vs. p = 0 gap is ~14 fL, far above the variation between draws.
stopifnot(
  fig6_late$mean_mcv[5] - fig6_late$mean_mcv[1] > 10,
  fig6_late$mean_mcv[4] > fig6_late$mean_mcv[2],
  fig6_late$mean_hbf[5] > fig6_late$mean_hbf[1]
)
```

# Per-participant estimates (Tables S2 and S4)

Pandey 2023 re-estimated the MCV and HbF parameters of each of the 40
participants after correcting their dosing profiles for inferred nonadherence
(Tables S2 and S4; Tables S1 and S3 hold the fits to the uncorrected pharmacy
profiles). Most of their medians are within a factor of two of the Pandey
2022 cohort medians used as the typical values. The feedback parameter Psi_e
and the stem-cell kill potency Kdse,50 differ several-fold: the 40 refitted
participants are a selected subgroup, and Kdse,50 is poorly determined
because both values sit far below the daily average concentration of about
40 uM, where stem-cell kill is near its maximum.

```{r per-participant}
s2 <- read.table(header = TRUE, text = "
id psi_rbc gamma_rbc kdsemax kdse50 kte kdemax kde50 alpha_mcv
1 9.0E+11 0.12 0.068 41.72 0.2913 0.014 859.49 0.325
2 7.2E+12 1.91 0.110 54.89 0.5474 0.027 948.49 0.390
3 1.8E+11 1.29 0.025 2.13 0.2270 0.040 516.24 1.124
4 8.0E+12 1.81 0.046 26.60 0.1588 0.025 809.04 0.372
5 1.1E+12 1.66 0.015 59.86 0.2146 0.018 955.42 0.260
6 3.3E+11 2.20 0.021 0.64 0.1212 0.033 439.12 0.438
7 1.7E+12 0.26 0.314 27.64 0.2026 0.011 775.36 0.631
8 1.9E+11 1.71 0.080 0.03 0.4718 0.024 563.99 0.340
9 3.3E+12 0.13 0.022 59.50 0.8048 0.016 573.20 0.263

  lapply(names(s2)[-1], function(p) data.frame(parameter = p, x = s2[[p]])),
  lapply(names(s4)[-1], function(p) data.frame(parameter = p, x = s4[[p]]))
) |>
  dplyr::group_by(parameter) |>
  dplyr::summarise(q1 = quantile(x, 0.25), median = median(x), q3 = quantile(x, 0.75), .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::mutate(typical_value = typical[parameter]) |>
  dplyr::arrange(match(parameter, names(typical)))
summ |>
  dplyr::rename(
    Parameter = parameter, "Q1 (2023)" = q1, "Median (2023)" = median,
    "Q3 (2023)" = q3, "Packaged typical value (2022 median)" = typical_value
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Corrected per-participant estimates of Pandey 2023 (Tables S2, S4) vs. the packaged typical values. psi_rbc in 10^12 cells/L.")
```

To simulate one of these participants, override the parameters on the log
scale. Below, the corrected estimates of participants 1-5 are run through the
typical participant's covariates, baselines and uninterrupted dosing, so the
spread reflects the parameters only (the participants' own baselines and
dosing records are not published).

```{r per-participant-sim}
ids <- 1:5
pars <- dplyr::inner_join(s2, s4, by = "id") |>
  dplyr::filter(id %in% ids) |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(-id, log)) |>
  dplyr::rename_with(~ paste0("l", .x), -id)
part_ev <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(ids, function(i) {
  make_regimen(i, sprintf("participant %d", i), days_all, n_days)
}))
part_sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod,
  events = dplyr::arrange(part_ev, id, time, dplyr::desc(evid)),
  params = dplyr::select(pars, -id), keep = "regimen", maxsteps = 1e6, hmax = 0.1
) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  dplyr::filter(time == round(time))
# Each participant's own kte must be in force (params rows map to ids in order).
kte_used <- part_sim |> dplyr::distinct(id, kte)
stopifnot(all(abs(kte_used$kte / s2$kte[match(kte_used$id, s2$id)] - 1) < 1e-8))
part_sim |>
  dplyr::select(time, regimen, `MCV (fL)` = MCV, `Mean cell HbF (pg)` = hbf_mc) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-c(time, regimen)) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, value, colour = regimen)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~name, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    x = "Time (days)", y = NULL, colour = NULL,
    title = "Participants 1-5 (Tables S2, S4) under uninterrupted dosing",
    caption = "Typical covariates, baselines and 20 mg/kg/day; not a replication of Figure 3."
  )
```

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Typical values come from the parent paper.** Pandey 2023 reports only
  per-participant estimates. The packaged values are the HUSTLE cohort central
  values of Pandey 2022, which fitted the same equations: means for the PK
  (Table 2) and medians for the pharmacodynamics (Tables 3 and 5). The
  per-parameter medians of the 2023 corrected estimates are compared with them
  in the table above. A set of per-parameter medians is not itself a fitted
  individual.
- **PK of the 2023 participants is not published.** Pandey 2023 reuses each
  participant's PK fit from Pandey 2022 without tabulating it; the cohort means
  of Pandey 2022 Table 2 are used.
- **Units of the daily average concentration.** Both papers plot the daily
  average concentration in ug/mL, while every concentration parameter of the
  pharmacodynamic model is reported per uM. The model converts with the molar
  mass of hydroxyurea (76.05 g/mol), which neither paper states. Using ug/mL
  directly would make the MCV rise `alpha C` about 13-fold smaller (0.37 x 3 =
  1 fL instead of 14 fL at 20 mg/kg), far below the 18 fL rise from baseline to
  6 months in Pandey 2022 Table 1.
- **Nadler blood volume.** Both papers print the height term of the Nadler
  equation as `height (cm)^3`, which gives blood volumes of about 10^5 L. The
  model uses height in metres, as in Nadler's equation; this reproduces the
  mean plasma volume of 1.77 L in Pandey 2022 Table 2 (1.89 L for the typical
  participant here).
- **Initial conditions.** The papers set the initial conditions from each
  participant's baseline data. The red-cell chain starts at its pre-treatment
  steady state, `Nse(0) = Ne1(0) = Ne2(0) = Ne3(0) = kde,max Ne(0) / kte`,
  which is the state implied by the printed `kpe,max` formula; the HbF
  intermediate starts at zero. Baselines are parameters whose typical values
  are the HUSTLE baseline means (Pandey 2022 Table 1).
- **Daily average concentration.** The source simulates the PK model each day
  and averages it. The model uses the equivalent closed form
  `F D / (ke Vp) / 1 day` for the day after each dose and zero for a day
  without one; the check above shows it equals the integral of the simulated
  profile. It assumes once-daily dosing and a dose that is cleared within the
  day (true for the typical half-life of 1.3 h).
- **Solver settings.** Multi-year daily-dosing simulations are run with
  `hmax = 0.1` (day) so the integrator resolves each day's absorption peak.
- **Hematocrit and body size** are covariates supplied by the user; the source
  updated them daily from clinic data. They are held constant here.
- **No variability.** The individual weighted-least-squares fits carry no
  between-subject variability or residual error model.
- **Figures 4-6** use a typical participant at 20 mg/kg/day; the representative
  participant of the paper (covariates, baselines, parameters and dose history)
  is not identified, so values differ while the patterns match.
- No erratum to either paper was found (checked 2026-10-26).
